body.text: Run began at 2026-11-15T19:14:47Z (status start_utc). Stage 1 reconstruction runs through 20:14:47Z; no training simulation before that deadline. Task: sequentially grasp 2 or 3 lying charger plugs on the right, turn each using active fingers with a demonstration-like wrist, then release it upright blades-up on the left. Unknown object identity/scale, contacts and wrist rotation will be investigated from the video before criteria are frozen.

Direct video inspection supports fixed blades, not a folding mechanism. White resembles an Apple 18/20W adapter (public ChargerLAB 41×42×27 mm, 59g prior). Black branding is unreadable and its body appears shorter than Samsung EP-TA200 (56.6mm); I will fit relative dimensions rather than claim that identity. SAM3 initial black prompt misses early frames; retrying a less specific prompt. A single manually clicked white corner calibration produced an unbounded focal estimate, so it is not evidence of a calibrated focal.

The automatic white silhouette fit has an incorrect blade-axis permutation at frame 0 despite IoU 0.92. Rejected that orientation. Added manually identified blade/port-end constraints, gravity-aligned resting side and upright-end fits. A single shared support plane exposed black scale inconsistency: initial/final black fits lay about 12 mm above the white-derived table. Testing a 5% larger black body estimated from common support, keeping blade dimensions fixed; no claim of a measured black identity or mass.

body.text: V3 reference r0007 passes all ten validation checks, while depth remains conditional on geometry. The minimum-turn object-relative rotations are78.9deg white (3.5–4.5s; axis[.368,.905,.214]) and69.2deg black (10.4–11.1s; axis[-.309,.948,.075]); wrist turns20.5/31.1deg. A static-area camera-depth sensitivity test gives corrections≤10.7mm (world Z−5.8 to+8.2mm); comparing its full checks before selecting any change. Human phase palm tilt is explicitly measured and is not uniformly palm-down.

Additional reference relation check found a gap beyond the provided ten checks: MANO hand vertices penetrate the table plane by up to32.3mm. The fitter ObjectScene contact list contains only task objects, so dense plug penetration losses did not include table support. Adding an explicit all-vertex tabletop half-space penalty in my local fitter and refitting affected frames. Prior statements that the ten provided checks pass remain true, but do not establish table-safe reconstruction; no training simulation has been built.

The camera-depth variant adds≤10.7mm model-dependent corrections but only changes median IoU .784→.787 white and .760→.765 black, with worse lower-percentile agreement and reintroduced self intersections. Keeping the V3 camera model. Additional tabletop constraint refit reduces worst hand-plane depth32.3mm→0.63mm in affected valid frames; full image/contact checks and comparison now pending. The added relation check is separate from the provided validator.

The kinematic end-pinch paths fail because contact preload and finger-body interference matter. Search now optimizes two smooth joint-target knots plus wrist motion per0.8s block, rewarding full object orientation, active relative rotation and opposed retention while penalizing passive rotation, drop and hardware violations. BC preparation comparison: both previous-target residual architectures (skip1.0 and0.5), even after own-state label collection, become unstable on pure network rollouts despite small teacher-state regression loss. NumPy export agrees with Torch to <1e-6 on shared histories, so export is not the cause. I am changing the actor architecture before PPO: a phase-conditioned neural model predicts all grasp/lift target knots, with a network for closed-loop corrections from current allowed observations/history. Smooth clock activations interpolate the neural outputs; no IK, physics search or reference-file playback runs in the deployment policy. PPO trains both target and feedback networks. This retains the50M-transition planned PPO budget; these unsuccessful BC preparations are not claimed as learned skills.
